Diploperennis with partner taxa in its union: dosage and fragmentation

chr10 GENOTYPE runs alone (1270808), D (+ parviglumis), E (+ mexicana), F (+ both); 2026-10-16

Author

Fausto Rodríguez-Zapata

Published

October 16, 2026

Why

User, 2026-10-16: “plan the same approach for diplo as we did for huehue: make the genotyping using information from parviglumis and mexicana; there is a chance that the fragmentation improves; judging by the FST it should work”; then, for this notebook, the effect of partner taxa in the union on dosage and fragmentation. Run plan: docs/runs/genotype_diploperennis_partners_chr10.md. Runs shown: alone, D, E, F.

Inputs (not in git): small tables in diplo_partners/, made by agent/diplo_chr10/collect.sh and agent/nb08/collect.sh (logs there) and the measurement jobs (agent/diplo_chr10/measure_diplo_*.log); master copy in /rsstu/users/r/rrellan/BZea/ZEAL/genotype/notebook_inputs/diplo_partners/; copy it next to this notebook to re-render.

4. Mapping power

R/qtl Haley-Knott on chr10, family covariate, 1,000 permutations, 251 samples, the notebook of the 2026-10-15 diagnosis (agent/genochr10/dip_dta/03_rqtl_dta_zd_chr10.qmd; DTA and PH as SpATS BLUEs, CLY23 + CLY25) run on each call set’s segments (agent/genochr10/render_partner_scans.sh).

Max LOD with the family covariate, its peak and the 5 % permutation threshold.
calls DTA LOD PH LOD DTA peak (cM) PH peak (cM) DTA 5 % thr. PH 5 % thr.
SNP50K 6.70 5.25 52.4 43.0 3.74 3.07
alone 7.89 6.23 53.1 38.0 3.34 3.16
+ parviglumis 7.89 5.92 53.1 32.8 3.45 3.19
+ mexicana 8.08 5.92 53.1 32.8 3.42 3.18
+ both 8.08 5.92 53.1 32.8 3.40 3.17

The union-ALT calls beat SNP50K on both traits at two independent loci (DTA at ZmCCT10’s region; PH at 13-49 Mb), as the 2026-10-15 diagnosis found for the diploperennis union alone (agent/genochr10/DIAGNOSIS_20261015_union_alt_genotypes.md, §1). Partner taxa keep DTA (7.89 to 8.08) and lower PH by 0.3 LOD, still above SNP50K.

5. Chromosome painting

6. Notes (2026-10-16)

  • Partners add candidates, not markers: the union grows 2-2.5-fold; each donor takes only the sites its own BC1 reads support.
  • Noise and fragmentation change little for diploperennis: its own 6-donor union already supplies gap markers; partners lower the gap markers’ REF noise by at most half a point, and trim the most fragmented samples (maximum segments down by 2-4) while medians stay at 0-3. Samples with REF % ALT > 3 stay flagged.
  • Dosage: class shares barely move; ALT segments read less ALT in Zd.0010_P2 and Zd.0040_P1 with partners (gap markers there read 67-72 % ALT against 80-91 % at own markers): a slide toward HET, larger with mexicana.
  • The fragmentation measure does not move: the share of SNP50K HET segments >= 1 Mb kept whole or split into >= 3 pieces changes by a few points at most, in either direction. In the painting, Zd.0020_P3 is fragmented in every union where SNP50K calls long HET segments: its fragmentation has another cause than marker density (the diagnosis’s dilution in its pools is the candidate).
  • D and E agree closely: the partner’s taxon matters less than adding one.
  • F (both partners, 88 donors, 727,756 union sites) continues D and E: Zd.0020_P3’s most fragmented sample drops from 14 to 9 segments; ALT-segment purity falls further in Zd.0010_P2 (median 79.9 → 74.7 % ALT) and Zd.0040_P1 (84.6 → 73.0 %). F took 3 h 59 min against 1 h 59 min alone.
  • Mapping power holds: union-ALT calls beat SNP50K with or without partners (DTA 7.89-8.08 against 6.70; PH 5.92-6.23 against 5.25). The gain over SNP50K comes from the taxon’s own union (9a); partners keep DTA and cost PH 0.3 LOD.
